title: Blue Cheese and Chive Popovers with Whipped Blue Cheese Butter
summary: Tall, crisp-shelled popovers studded with blue cheese and chives, hollow and airy inside, served warm with a blue cheese butter.
equipment: 6-hole popover tin or deep muffin tin

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Butter
steps.text: Mash 115 g butter with 55 g blue cheese, 4 tbsp chives and black pepper and set aside.

steps.title: Prep
steps.text: Brush a popover tin with oil and wipe out the excess.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 190 g bread flour, 3 tbsp chives, 1½ tsp mustard powder, ¾ tsp salt and a pinch of cayenne.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Beat 360 ml warm milk with 3 eggs until frothy, pour into the dry ingredients and whisk until mostly smooth.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Leave the batter 10 min, then stir in 55 g blue cheese.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Divide among the tin holes and bake at 200 °C without opening the door until tall and deep golden, 40-45 min.

steps.title: Vent
steps.text: Pierce each top with a skewer and bake 5 min more, then serve at once with the blue cheese butter.

tips: Warm the milk and eggs before whisking in, as this helps the popovers rise tall.
Resist opening the oven door while baking so the popovers don't collapse.
Pierce the tops with a skewer near the end of baking to let steam escape and keep them crisp.
storage: Best served warm straight from the oven, as popovers lose their crisp texture on standing. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
